column1: # The starred reference corpus: a SECOND sample, drawn to compare against reference-corpus.tsv rather than to
# replace it. Same seed, same discipline, same draw script, one qualifier different.
#   language:Java fork:false mirror:false size:>=1000 stars:>=50 created:<2026-08-21
# WHY A SECOND SAMPLE. The uniform draw in reference-corpus.tsv is dominated by coursework and hobby
# projects — ten of ten with zero stars and no licence. Those write `id`, `get`, `name` and `value`, which is
# what the reference is for. They may not write `log`, `license`, `builder` or `optional`, which are what
# MAINTAINED projects share, and all nine evaluation-set members are maintained. Whether the denominator has
# to resemble the code being read is a question about the reference, and two samples answer it where an
# argument does not.
# `stars:>=50` selects for attention rather than for content, so it does not breach the rule the first
# manifest states. IT IS NOT NEUTRAL EITHER, and the cost is measurable rather than suspected:
#   frame            size        median repository created
# Stars accumulate, so a repository needs years to reach fifty, and this frame's yearly counts peak in 2016
# and fall to 302 by 2026 where the uniform frame's rise to 2025. Four years older at the median: Java from
# before records, before `var` was ordinary, with streams still arriving. So this sample trades a maturity
# gap for an age gap. NEITHER FRAME IS THE NEUTRAL ONE, which is why each reference's claim is reported
# separately rather than pooled into one number.
# THE COMPOSITION, stated before anything was read, from the repositories' own descriptions:
#   gedcom4j                 a library for reading and writing genealogy files
#   protect                  a platform for robust threshold cryptography
#   akarnokd-misc            miscellaneous implementations, by an RxJava contributor
#   aimsicdl                 an Android IMSI-catcher detector
#   krgallery                Android cropping, video and photos
#   flycolabelview           an Android label widget
#   plugintheme              Android theme switching
#   light-novel-library      an Android reader for a light-novel site
#   cloud2020                SpringCloud teaching material
#   estruturadedadosjavadio  Java data-structures course work
#   FIVE OF THE TEN ARE ANDROID and two are teaching material, so this sample is not maintained server-side
#   Java either. Between the two manifests the reading has a coursework denominator and an Android
#   denominator, and NEITHER RESEMBLES THE EVALUATION-SET MEMBERS, which are Apache-shaped libraries and
#   servers. A third frame drawn from repositories that publish an artefact would, and is not drawn here
#   because a frame is stated before it is drawn and this one was stated before these rows existed.
#   Four of the ten state a licence — two GPL-2.0, one GPL-3.0, one MIT — against none of the uniform ten.
#   A repository is read, never redistributed, so copyleft is recorded rather than refused, as jPOS is in
#   evaluation-set.tsv. Nothing was rejected: all ten ranks the seed produced were accepted, first time.
# Columns, the draw, the rejection policy and the doctrine argument are all as reference-corpus.tsv states
# them; only the frame differs. The draw and its record are docs/reference-corpus/draw.py and
# docs/reference-corpus/draw-starred.json.
